     1	# Poetry plugin to Pin Path dependencies
     2	
     3	[![Poetry](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://python-poetry.org/badge/v0.json)](https://python-poetry.org/)
     4	[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/gerbenoostra/poetry-plugin-mono-repo-deps/graph/badge.svg?token=O6NQ6H0IVN)](https://codecov.io/gh/gerbenoostra/poetry-plugin-mono-repo-deps)
     5	
     6	A [**Poetry**](https://python-poetry.org/) plugin for Poetry mono repositories, that will replace path dependencies with named dependency specifications.
     7	
     8	A mono repository contains multiple Python packages, which can depend on each other.
     9	These are typically path dependencies with the `develop = true` attribute.
    10	This allows for easy development and local running.
    11	However, when the packages are published to a PyPi repo, these dependencies should be named dependencies.
    12	By publishing the packages with named dependencies, one can easily install the packages and their dependencies.
    13	
    14	This plugin will replace path dependencies (`name @ path`) with named dependency specifications (`name ~= version`).
    15	By default, this is done when building artifacts ([`poetry build`](https://python-poetry.org/docs/main/cli/#build)) and exporting the locked dependency list ([`poetry export`](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-plugin-export)).
    16	The plugin can however be configured to modify any other command registered by Poetry or other plugins.
    17	
    18	## An example using build and export
    19	
    20	Suppose you have a single folder with 2 Python packages, where one (`app-b`) depends on the other (`lib-a`).
    21	
    22	The used library has the following in its Poetry section:
    23	
    24	```toml
    25	# repo/A/pyproject.toml
    26	[tool.poetry]
    27	name = "lib-a"
    28	version = "0.0.1"
    29	```
    30	
    31	The application package depends on the previous library as follows:
    32	
    33	```toml
    34	# repo/B/pyproject.toml
    35	[tool.poetry]
    36	name = "app-B"
    37	
    38	[tool.poetry.dependencies]
    39	library-a = {path = "../A", develop=true}
    40	```
    41	
    42	### Poetry build
    43	
    44	By default, building the above project with Poetry (`poetry build`), will result in a build artifact (`tar.gz`/`whl`) containing a path dependency in its metadata similar to:
    45	
    46	```
    47	Requires-Dist: lib-a @ file:///your/local/checkout/project/root/lib-a
    48	```
    49	
    50	This prevents sharing the build and reusing the build artifact on other systems, as it expects to find `lib-a` at that specific path.
    51	
    52	Using this Mono-Repo-Deps plugin, the Poetry build will result in the following dependency:
    53	
    54	```
    55	Requires-Dist: lib-a (>=0.0.1,<0.1.0)
    56	```
    57	
    58	### Poetry export
    59	
    60	By default, exporting the full dependency list (`poetry export`) results in a dependency list (`requirements.txt`) that also contain path dedendencies with full paths:
    61	
    62	```
    63	lib-a @ file:///your/local/checkout/project/root/lib-a
    64	```
    65	
    66	Again, by using this Mono-Repo-Deps plugin, these will become:
    67	
    68	```
    69	lib-a==0.1.0
    70	```
    71	
    72	## Installation
    73	
    74	You can install the plugin as explained in the [Poetry documentation about plugin usage](https://python-poetry.org/docs/main/plugins/#using-plugins).
    75	
    76	Which can be summarized as:
    77	
    78	If you used PipX to install Poetry:
    79	
    80	```shell
    81	pipx inject poetry poetry-plugin-mono-repo-deps
    82	```
    83	
    84	If you used Pip to install Poetry:
    85	
    86	```shell
    87	pip install poetry-plugin-mono-repo-deps
    88	```
    89	
    90	On non-Windows devices, you can also use Poetry's `self add` which will also validate compatibility:
    91	
    92	```shell
    93	poetry self add poetry-plugin-mono-repo-deps
    94	```
    95	
    96	## Usage:
    97	
    98	As plugins are installed systemwide, **this plugin is by default disabled** to not unintentionally modify the existing behavior of Poetry.
    99	
   100	Enable the plugin by adding the following (empty) section to your `pyproject.toml`:
   101	
   102	```toml
   103	# repo/B/pyproject.toml
   104	[tool.poetry-monorepo.deps]
   105	```
   106	
   107	This is equivalent to adding the following default settings:
   108	
   109	```toml
   110	[tool.poetry-monorepo.deps]
   111	enabled = true
   112	commands = ["build", "export"]
   113	constraint = "~="
   114	source_types = ["file", "directory"]
   115	only_develop = false
   116	```
   117	
   118	Possible alternative values can be found in the following section:
   119	
   120	## Configuration:
   121	
   122	### `enabled`
   123	
   124	**Type**: `boolean`
   125	
   126	**Default**: `true`
   127	
   128	**Allowed values**: `true`, `false`
   129	
   130	Whether the plugin should be activated for commands on this project.
   131	
   132	### `commands`
   133	
   134	**Type**: `List[string]`
   135	
   136	**Default**: `["build", "export"]`
   137	
   138	**Allowed values**: Any CLI command registered with Poetry (could also be provided by other plugins).
   139	
   140	The intercepted poetry commands.
   141	The plugin will intercept the command and update the internal representation of dependencies, changing the path dependencies to named dependency specifications.
   142	
   143	### `constraint`
   144	
   145	**Type**: `string`
   146	
   147	**Default**: `~=`
   148	
   149	**Allowed values**: `==`, `>=` , `~=` , `^` (All [valid Poetry version constraints](https://python-poetry.org/docs/dependency-specification/)).
   150	
   151	The version constraint that is applied to the current version of the dependency.
   152	
   153	For example, when the dependency has version `0.0.1`, and the default constraint string `~=` is used, it will result in a named dependency with version `>=0.1.0, <0.1.0`.
   154	
   155	### `source_types`
   156	
   157	**Type**: `List[string]`
   158	
   159	**Default**: `["file", "directory"]` (local Path dependencies)
   160	
   161	**Allowed values**: `["file", "directory", "url", "git"]`. (Any `source_type` attribute of Poetry's internal Dependency object, which includes the lowercase VCS identifier, like `git`).
   162	
   163	The type of dependencies that should be replaced with their named version specification.
   164	
   165	### `only_develop`
   166	
   167	**Type**: `boolean`
   168	
   169	**Default**: `false`
   170	
   171	Enable to only replace `develop` dependencies, which, as currently implemented in Poetry, are only `directory` [Path dependencies](https://python-poetry.org/docs/main/dependency-specification/#path-dependencies).
   172	
   173	This filter is **only applied to directory path** dependencies, as only those can have the `develop` mark.
   174	
   175	If you configure `source_types` to be any Path dependency (ie. `file` or `directory`), all file path dependencies will be translated, while only the directory dependencies annotated with `develop = true` will be translated.
   176	
   177	## Caveats
   178	
   179	Currently, the plugin has only been verified to work with the `poetry build` and `poetry export` commands.
   180	Though theoretically it should work with any other (plugin's) command, your mileage may vary.
   181	
   182	## How it works
   183	
   184	If enabled, this plugin registers itself to run before specific commands.
   185	When these commands are run, it will modify the internal lock file representation that Poetry uses, replacing the path dependency objects with regular dependencies.
   186	
   187	The idea came from the [Python Poetry Monorepo without Limitations](https://gerben-oostra.medium.com/python-poetry-mono-repo-without-limitations-dd63b47dc6b8) blog post on Medium, which describes how a simple script can modify the `pyproject.toml` before a build step, resulting in named dependencies in the build artifacts.
   188	This plugin only temporarily modifies the structure, in memory, just for the command you run it on.
   189	
   190	## Contributing
   191	
   192	We recommend using PyEnv to select the right Python version:
   193	
   194	```console
   195	pyenv local && poetry env use $(which python)
   196	make venv
   197	```
   198	
   199	We use [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/), which most recent version requires Python >=3.9, while this project aims to work on Python >=3.8.
   200	Therefore install pre-commit on your system yourself (using Homebrew / PipX)
   201	
   202	Tests can be run with `make test`, linting with `make lint`
   203
